The professor mentioned contamination in the **Isolation Forest** lecture on **2026-11-06**. 

At **[21:29]** in the recording, the professor said:

> "In the demo I set contamination to 0.05, so the model flags the top five percent of points as anomalies. Set it too high and you start flagging normal data."

This refers to the `contamination` parameter in Isolation Forest, which controls what percentage of data points to treat as anomalies. Setting it too high causes the model to incorrectly flag normal data as anomalies.
